title: Automated Tenant Incident Orchestration and Remediation Playbook
author: Leah Kim
body:
Overview

This playbook documents the end-to-end automated orchestration and manual handoff procedures used by Redwood Customer Success and Support to detect, remediate, and verify tenant-level incidents with minimal customer impact. It is intended for use during production incidents that affect a single tenant or a small cohort of tenants (not full platform outages). The goal is to resolve service-impacting problems within the tenant SLO window or apply safe fallbacks that preserve availability while engineering diagnoses root causes.

When to use this playbook

- Tenant-facing degradation detected by telemetry (latency, errors, KV-cache regressions, model-quality signals).
- Sudden unit-cost spikes or quota exhaustion that threaten availability.
- Failed automated model upgrade rollouts that affect a tenant.
- Routing and network flakiness isolated to a customer’s region or private deployment link.

Scope and ownership

- Primary owner: Customer Success (tenant stability squad).
- Secondary owner: Eng-Platform (runtime orchestration).
- On-call escalation: Dedicated SRE for the affected region.
- This playbook covers: detection signals, enrichment, automated remediation actions, verification tests, escalation thresholds, and post-incident RCA inputs.

Key SLOs and thresholds (tenant-level)

- Availability: 99.9% (per-tenant request success, 5xx < 0.1%).
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for short text generation (<= 256 tokens); alert if p95 increases by >20% over baseline for 5 minutes.
- Cost: unit-token cost deviation > 40% triggers investigation.
- KV-cache hit-rate: fall below 70% sustained for 3 minutes -> alert.

Automated detection signals (examples)

- Telemetry rule: p95_latency_tenant > baseline * 1.2 for 5m.
- Error spike: 5xx_rate_tenant > 0.5% sustained for 3m.
- Token-cost spike: token_cost_rate per-minute increases > 40%.
- Model-quality regressions: eval-alerts flagged by tenant’s eval set (similarity loss or hallucination metric).
- Networking: TLS handshake failure rate or connection resets > 1% absolute.

Enrichment pipeline (what automation performs before action)

1. Correlate tenant signals with model, route, and infra pool (tags: model_id, route_id, pool_id).
2. Attach last 2 minutes of request traces (sampled).
3. Run quick synthetic check against tenant route (see Verification tests).
4. Generate incident stub in incident system with priority recommendation and suggested remediation.

Automated remediation actions (ordered by safety)

- Action A: Tenant read-only traffic shaping for non-critical routes
  - Purpose: reduce cost and limit degradation scope while preserving critical API calls.
  - Command example: curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.example/v1/tenants/T-123/traffic-shape -d '{"mode":"critical-only","expiry":"15m"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'

- Action B: Switch tenant routing policy to fallback model variant
  - Purpose: move traffic to a compatible smaller/quantized model to restore latency and availability.
  - Safe variants must be pre-approved in tenant config.
  - CLI example: rwdctl tenants route-set --tenant T-123 --route fallback --model redwood/small-2b-q4f

- Action C: Promote tenant to reserved capacity (burst)
  - Purpose: temporary capacity allocation from dedicated pools. Requires entitlement check.
  - API example: POST /ops/tenants/T-123/reserve-capacity {"pool":"dedicated-gnx-1","duration":"30m"}

- Action D: KV cache warm-up/restore script
  - Purpose: rehydrate prefix cache to reduce cold-start token costs and latency.
  - Script snippet:
    #!/bin/bash
    REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
    python tools/rehydrate_cache.py --tenant T-123 --sample-size 500

- Action E: Quiesce long-running background jobs (embedding indexes, reindexes)
  - Purpose: stop noisy background workloads temporarily to reduce contention.
  - Note: notify customer success and log action.

Automated decision logic (simplified)

- If p95_latency > 20% and 5xx_rate < 0.5% -> run cache-warmup + synthetic test.
- If 5xx_rate >= 0.5% -> immediate route switch to fallback model and notify SRE.
- If token_cost_spike && cost deviation > 40% -> apply traffic-shape (critical-only) and schedule FinOps review.

Runbook: Incident lifecycle (detailed steps)

1) Detection and enrichment (automated)
   - Telemetry rule fires -> enrichment workflow runs and creates incident stub.
   - System posts summary in #cs-ops and creates a PagerDuty alert if priority >= P2.

2) Immediate automated remediation (0-5 minutes)
   - Orchestration engine evaluates tenant policy and executes the highest-safety remediation allowed.
   - Record every action with an audit log and create reversible change unit.

3) Verification (5-15 minutes)
   - Automated synthetic verification executes the tenant’s smoke tests and records p50/p95, error-rate, and a small token-cost sample.
   - If verification passes, incident moves to ‘stabilizing’. If not, escalate to on-call SRE.

4) Manual escalation and deeper mitigation (15-60 minutes)
   - On-call SRE inspects traces and profile data, may perform pool-scale out, failover to another region, or trigger a model rollback.
   - Customer Success prepares proactive customer communication templates (see Communications section).

5) Post-stabilization (60m+)
   - Open an RCA task and schedule triage meeting if impact > 1 hour or > 5% request loss.
   - Re-run tenant evals on the pre/post request samples.

Verification tests (automated)

- Smoke script (example):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_KEY' \\n    -d '{"model":"current","input":"SYNTHETIC_SMOKE_PROMPT","max_tokens":64}' | jq '{status: .status, latency_ms: .latency_ms}'

- Synthetic assertions:
  | Assertion | Threshold | Action if fail |
  |---|---:|---|
  | p95 latency | <= baseline * 1.2 | escalate to SRE |
  | 5xx rate | < 0.5% | route fallback |
  | KV cache hit | >= 70% | initiate rehydrate script |

- Canary traffic replay: reply last-30s of tenant requests against fallback route in an isolated sandbox. Verify token usage and output quality against tenant eval set.

Communication templates (quick copy)

- Customer alert (short):
  Subject: Temporary mitigation applied to your Redwood tenant (T-123)
  Body: 
  Hi <CustomerName>,

  We detected degraded performance on your tenant and applied a temporary mitigation (fallback routing / rate shaping) to protect availability. Our engineers are investigating — we will share updates every 15 minutes. If you need escalation, reply with URGENT.

- Internal update: 
  Incident T-123 - automated mitigation applied: fallback routing -> redwood/small-2b-q4f; verification passed at 09:42 UTC. Owner: Leah Kim.

Operational requirements and permissions (table)

| Permission | Minimum Role | Required by automation |
|---|---|---|
| tenants.route-set | ops-runbooks | Yes |
| tenants.reserve-capacity | ops-admin | Conditional |
| telemetry.read | monitoring | Yes |
| incidents.create | cs-ops | Yes |

Rollout, testing and guardrails

- Feature toggles: automated remediation must be behind a feature flag per-region and per-tenant. Default: off for first 7 days after tenant creation.
- Staging tests: weekly synthetic stress tests that exercise fallback routing and cache rehydration.
- Safety limits: automation may not change encryption/keying configs or customer-provided model artifacts.

Audit and observability

- Every automated change writes a change-event to the audit log with: actor=automation, reason=trigger-rule-id, actions=[...], revert-token.
- Metrics to monitor: automation_success_rate, automation_false_positive_rate, manual_override_count. Target: automation_success_rate >= 90% and false_positive_rate < 5%.

Escalation matrix (summary)

- P3: automated mitigation succeeded, customer notified by CS -> owner: CS on-call.
- P2: automation applied but verification failed -> owner: regional SRE on-call. PagerDuty P2.
- P1: platform-wide cross-tenant impact or data-loss suspected -> company-wide incident; follow incident-response runbook in eng-sre.

Post-incident activities

1. Immediate actions (within 24h):
   - Confirm revert of temporary changes if not needed.
   - Export request and trace samples and attach to incident.

2. 72-hour follow-up:
   - Run tenant-level replays against production and canary models to validate regression fixes.
   - Create RCA draft and assign owners for remedial engineering work.

3. QBR inputs:
   - Capture impact window, affected customers, mitigation timeline, and cost delta. Include synthetic verification artifacts and automation logs.

Testing checklist (before enabling automation for a customer)

- [ ] Tenant has a validated fallback model listed in tenant config.
- [ ] Customer consents to automated traffic shaping and temporary model switch (contract flag).
- [ ] Entitlements for reserve-capacity are defined and funded under the contract.
- [ ] Integration test passed: synthetic smoke + replay pass in staging.

Appendices and snippets

A. Sample orchestration policy (JSON):
{ "tenant_id": "T-123", "triggers": ["p95_latency>baseline*1.2", "5xx_rate>0.5"], "actions": ["cache_rehydrate", "route_fallback", "traffic_shape"], "rollback_ttl": 30 }

B. Example timeline entry for incident stub:
- 09:10 UTC: telemetry rule fired (p95 latency +22%)
- 09:11 UTC: automation executed cache_rehydrate (audit_id=AU-981)
- 09:12 UTC: synthetic verification failed p95 -> automation escalated to route_fallback (audit_id=AU-982)
- 09:17 UTC: verification passed; incident marked stabilizing

Related pages and references

- Tenant stability predictive signals runbook (telemetry rules and thresholds).
- Eng-platform runbooks: automated-rollbacks and audit-log-format.

Ownership and review cadence

- Playbook owner: Leah Kim (Customer Success).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any automation false-positive > 3% in a quarter.
- Reviewers: Omar Patel (SRE), Ruth Alvarez (Eng Platform), Marcus Chen (FinOps).
